clue.text: Paper putting out leader about accommodation

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the remaining letters round to face the other way
the paper's name loses its leading letter, the one at the front

parts.note: The Times is a newspaper, so paper gives its name

explanation.surface: A newspaper drops its editorial to write about housing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting out leader' removes T from TIMES, leaving IMES; 'about' turns that round. 'Leader' looks like a newspaper's editorial, but here it just means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi is a semi-detached house, a common type of British home, so it counts as accommodation.

clue.text: Final message after school game — that's the spirit!

indicators.note: after means the final message comes after the school and game pieces

parts.note: nap is a card game, short for Napoleon
PS, postscript, is a final message added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A school game ends with a cheery final message of encouragement.
explanation.walkthrough: Nap is a card game. 'that's the spirit!' looks like a cheer, but it simply points to a strong drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnapps is a strong distilled alcoholic drink, which is a spirit.

clue.text: After short time, a politician can be threatening

indicators.note: after puts the article and politician after the short time

parts.note: min is the abbreviation for minute, a short time
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician can turn menacing after only a short time.
explanation.definitionFit: Minatory is a formal adjective meaning menacing or threatening.

clue.text: University male gets married — none the worse for it?

parts.note: paired, coupled up, as a married couple are

explanation.surface: A male student marries and is apparently none the worse for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being undamaged or undiminished is having come off none the worse for an experience.

clue.text: Occasion not nice it turned out

indicators.note: turned out suggests the letters are shaken up, with the word it put out of the mix

explanation.surface: An event that was unpleasant, as it turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' works as a composite: the letters of NOT NICE are those of the answer plus IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonce means the present occasion, as in the phrase for the nonce.

clue.text: Language we don't often hear — it turns up just the same

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up means read from bottom to top, and just the same says it is unchanged

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A rarely heard language comes along all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: The word reads the same both ways, so turned up a down light it is unchanged. It is the language of Kerala in south India.
explanation.definitionFit: Malayalam is a Dravidian language of southern India, rarely heard in Britain.

clue.text: Customers may have been stung when they bought it

definitions.text: Customers may have been stung when they bought it

parts.words: Customers may have been stung when they bought it
parts.note: stung means bitten by insects, not overcharged, so buyers wanted relief from the sting

explanation.surface: Shoppers were overcharged for a purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: Stung looks like slang for ripped off; it means stung by a bee or wasp, hence a medicine for the reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: This drug counters allergic reactions, including the swelling and itching after an insect sting.

clue.text: Attacked funding being received by Communist

indicators.note: being received by means the funding word is taken inside the communist word

parts.note: red is the traditional label for a communist
aid is financial help or funding

explanation.surface: A Communist taking money was assaulted.
explanation.walkthrough: Red is the traditional colour, and so the nickname, of communists.
explanation.definitionFit: To raid is to make a sudden attack, so raided means attacked.

clue.text: Elegant groom — the ultimate for matrimony

parts.note: to groom is to dress or smarten someone up

indicators.note: the ultimate for means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A smart bridegroom is the last word in married life.
explanation.walkthrough: Groom looks like a bridegroom but is the verb, to smarten; 'the ultimate for' takes Y from matrimony.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressy describes stylish, smart clothing, so it means elegant.

clue.text: Suspenders not seen in Britain since the sixties?

definitions.text: Suspenders not seen in Britain since the sixties?

parts.words: Suspenders not seen in Britain since the sixties?
parts.note: read suspenders as people who suspend others by the neck, the executioners Britain stopped using after abolishing capital punishment in 1965

explanation.surface: Stockings-and-suspenders fashion supposedly vanished from Britain after the sixties.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests stocking suspenders; really it means executioners who hang people, out of work since Britain abolished the death penalty in 1965.
explanation.definitionFit: Executioners suspend the condemned from a rope, and Britain's last hangings were in 1964.

clue.text: Bungle made by teacher detaining boy over dress?

indicators.note: detaining means the teacher word holds the other pieces inside it, as a pupil is kept in

parts.note: a master is a schoolteacher

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the boy word stands above the dress word

parts.note: lad is a boy
a mini is a short dress

explanation.surface: A teacher keeps a boy in for his dress, and makes a mess of it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light 'over' puts the boy above the dress; 'detaining' plays on a teacher keeping a pupil in.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer something badly is to bungle or mismanage it.

clue.text: Room framed by the French type of tracery

indicators.note: framed by means the room word sits inside the French article, enclosed on both sides

parts.note: le is the French word for the
an attic is a room under the roof

explanation.surface: A room bordered by French ornamental tracery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French' is a common crossword device for the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: Lattice is a criss-cross pattern of strips, a kind of openwork tracery seen in windows and screens.

clue.text: Major road blocked by hostile guns

indicators.note: blocked by means the road word has the hostile word lodged inside it, like an obstruction

parts.note: an artery is a main road, a major traffic route
ill as in ill will, unfriendly or hostile

explanation.surface: A major road is barricaded by enemy guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major road' tempts as a motorway abbreviation, but here it is the longer word for a main route.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery is the collective term for large guns used in warfare.

clue.text: Dastardly types in lists

definitions.meaning: to list is to lean over to one side, as a ship does

explanation.definitionFit: Heel is slang for a cad, and a ship heels when it leans or lists to one side.

clue.text: Asteroids, pal, could bring disaster on cosmic scale

indicators.note: could bring suggests the letters of the two words may produce something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: An astronomer warns a friend that asteroids could cause a cosmic disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could bring' rearranges the letters of ASTEROIDS and PAL. The title is Milton's epic poem about the fall of Satan and of humankind.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's epic tells of Satan's fall and humanity's expulsion from Eden, a catastrophe on a cosmic scale.

clue.text: Illegitimate children? A red herring

definitions.meaning: children born on the side, offspring of an affair, read as issue on the side
a distraction from the main point under discussion

explanation.definitionFit: A matter of secondary importance diverts attention like a red herring; read literally, it is offspring born on the side.

clue.text: Name bird, and make observation about it

indicators.note: about means the observation word goes around the bird word

parts.note: to note is to observe or remark
mina is a variant spelling of myna, an Asian starling

explanation.surface: Name a bird and write a note about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird is the myna, in its less common spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate someone is to name them for a post or award.

clue.text: Not being fair with a girl?

definitions.text: Not being fair with a girl?

parts.words: Not being fair with a girl?
parts.note: fair means blonde, not just, so this is a girl whose hair is dark

explanation.surface: Someone treats his girlfriend unjustly.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair suggests justice; it means fair-haired, so the girl in question has dark hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the feminine form for a woman with dark brown hair, the opposite of a blonde.

clue.text: Maiden is gloomy about bloke's last vile wrongdoing

parts.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
taken as written

indicators.note: about means the gloomy word goes around the following pieces

parts.note: dour means stern and gloomy

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word bloke's

parts.note: mean as in base or vile

explanation.surface: A gloomy girl rails against some man's latest vile misdeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' takes E from bloke's; E plus MEAN go 'about'-wise inside DOUR to make DEMEANOUR, after M and IS. M for maiden is a cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A misdemeanour is a minor crime or misdeed, a piece of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Northern town pub getting over dispute

indicators.note: getting over in a down clue puts the pub word above the dispute word

parts.note: a bar is a pub or drinking place
a row is a quarrel or dispute

explanation.surface: A northern pub is recovering from a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Barrow-in-Furness is a shipbuilding town in Cumbria, north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrow-in-Furness, usually just called Barrow, is a town in Cumbria in northern England.

clue.text: Bird nibbled a morsel

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
bit, past tense of bite, as in nibbled

explanation.surface: A bird pecked at a tasty scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A titbit is a small tasty piece of food, a morsel.

clue.text: Fib I laugh about — incomplete excuse

indicators.note: about tells us to read the selected letters backwards
incomplete means only part of the run of letters in these words is used

explanation.surface: Someone laughs at their own lie, which turns out to be a half-baked excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' takes IBILA from inside the letters of 'Fib I laugh'; 'about' turns it round. 'Fib' tempts as the definition, but the definition is 'excuse'.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, used as an excuse to escape blame.

clue.text: Hunch during university lesson

parts.note: in means during, as in in the morning
tuition is teaching, the kind of lesson paid for at university

explanation.surface: A student gets a hunch in the middle of a lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: Intuition is an instinctive feeling, the same as a hunch.

clue.text: Junk food

definitions.meaning: the stomach lining of a cow or sheep, eaten as a dish

explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is cooked cow's stomach eaten as a dish, and slang for nonsense or rubbish.

clue.text: Monies having to be sent back as enclosure?

definitions.text: Monies having to be sent back as enclosure?

parts.words: Monies having to be sent back as enclosure?
parts.note: money handed back to a payer, such as a refund cheque slipped into a letter and posted back

explanation.surface: Refunds have to be returned in an envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebate is a partial refund, money paid back to someone who has overpaid.

clue.text: Wide of the mark in performance, no longer retained

indicators.note: retained means the former-partner word is held within the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
an act is a performance on stage
ex means former, no longer what one was

explanation.surface: A performance went off the mark and the actor was no longer kept on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer' gives the prefix for former, as in ex-wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inexact is imprecise, so it misses or is wide of the mark.

clue.text: As it goes up the banks may be threatened

definitions.text: As it goes up the banks may be threatened

parts.words: As it goes up the banks may be threatened
parts.note: the banks are river banks at risk of flooding, not financial institutions facing a crisis

explanation.surface: Financial banks worry as interest rates or some index climb.
explanation.walkthrough: Banks suggests money; really they are a river's banks, which flood when the height of the water rises.
explanation.definitionFit: The height of a river's surface, when it rises, threatens to overflow its banks.

clue.text: One giving foundation to "English"

parts.note: a bed is a base or foundation, as in a bed of concrete

explanation.surface: Someone who laid the foundations of English.
explanation.walkthrough: The Venerable Bede, an Anglo-Saxon monk, wrote the first history of the English people, so he founded English history; BED is placed under E as a base.
explanation.definitionFit: The monk Bede is called the father of English history, a founding figure of English learning.
